title: Systems that cannot stop: windows, contracts and SLAs

videos.script: Some systems at Serra Alta may never stop. {{trucks}} Milk is collected on every day of the year, and a truck that does not come means milk poured away. Other systems stop on purpose. {{calendar}} SAP goes down every Sunday morning for maintenance, and for five working days a month it belongs to the people closing the books. Between those two kinds of system run about a hundred and ten integrations. Until now, nobody had written down what any of them promised. {{chain}} So this lesson starts with arithmetic. Three systems in a row, each one above ninety-nine per cent. The checkout they serve together is down for almost six days a year. Then the words that turn a number into a promise: a measurement, a target, and a contract with consequences. {{contract}} Joana writes the first interface contracts, and she puts every window and every freeze on one calendar. {{fallback}} Then come the questions nobody enjoys. What does each system do when the one it depends on is gone? And how much data can you afford to lose while you bring it back?
